subject: phoenix
pitch: A phoenix rising with its wings flung open. Feathers blaze from deep crimson at the body through orange to golden yellow at the tips, a crest of flame-shaped plumes on its head, long trailing tail feathers like ribbons of fire, glowing amber eyes and a golden hooked beak. Embers and sparks drift off its wings.
reasoning:
I'm planning a deterministic TypeScript module using the SDK, carefully scoped to valid API features, modeling a phoenix with wings spread and body elevated off the ground to convey a rising pose.

Setting up the orientation with head facing forward and tail back, wings spanning sideways, and sketching the overall part structure using the builder's joint, chain, sweep, membrane, and card primitives while double-checking each function's correct signature before writing.

I'm planning to use gradient paints for feather coloring, transitioning from deep crimson at the roots to gold at the tips, and sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting with hips as the root joint in model space.

Now I'm mapping out the spine chain as a short catmull path from hips up through the torso, then continuing into neck and head joints, defining each segment's position and orientation to build the forward-facing posture before adding a jaw joint as a child of the head.

For the tail, I'm planning a fan of three long feather plumes swept along separate catmull paths flaring out from the hip base, tapering the radius toward the tips and applying a fire-gradient paint, with each plume tied to an articulated tail bone chain for flexibility.

Now for the wings, each is a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to fingertip, positioned flung open and slightly raised, with joint names shoulderL, elbowL, wristL, fingerL for the left side.

I'm working out the wing membrane: it stretches between the leading-edge chain and a trailing feather path from body to tip, taking a gradient paint for color across the surface.

For feathers, I'm deciding between extruded flame-shaped outlines positioned along the trailing edge, oriented so their plane spans the wing's span direction and chord direction, versus a card-based approach with flow textures. I'll go with extruded feathers laid flat in the horizontal wing plane so they read naturally from above.

That orientation matches what I want: feather length along the chord, spacing across the span, thickness vertical. For the primaries, I'll place roughly six feathers along the trailing edge at span positions from 0.3 to 0.95, computing each one's position by lerping along the wing chain with a slight backward offset.

Actually simpler to use a trailing-edge path built from a few literal points, since those come with no bone and inherit the nearest joint automatically — that avoids fiddly offset math while still giving reasonable feather placement.

I'm laying out literal coordinates for the left wing's main chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip) and a separate trailing-edge path for the membrane's back edge, then placing primary feathers at sampled points along that trailing edge so their bases sit on the membrane and extend backward.

Now I'm defining a flame-shaped outline function for each feather, with points marked "sharp" at the tip, then extruding that outline along the feather's base-to-tip direction with a gradient color running from deep crimson at the base to golden at the tip.

I'm picking out my color palette—crimson, red, orange, gold, amber for the body and beak, keeping everything in bright standard-material tones since emissive isn't an option. Now I'm planning the body's construction via a swept spine path with radii, gradient-colored from the hips to the neck.

Working out the radius function...

For the neck I'll sweep along its chain with a tapering radius from about 0.09 to 0.06, letting it follow the chain's bones. For the head, I'm considering using a sphere part attached to the head bone with a slight forward/up offset instead of another sweep, scaling it for the right shape.

I'm placing the eyes as small amber spheres positioned relative to the head's local coordinates, using the left/right offsets so they mirror symmetrically. For the beak, I'm sweeping a bezier curve anchored to the head bone with a tapering radius ending in a sharp hooked point, using flat and pointed caps to get that raptor-like profile.

I'm planning the lower beak as a shorter sweep attached to the jaw joint, then designing the crest as a fan of flame-shaped plumes extending from the top of the head, sweeping backward and upward with thin tapering radii to mimic feather tufts.

Writing crest extrude params...

Normalizing the direction vector before passing it in...

For feathers I'm keeping x and y orthogonal unit vectors along the wing plane, and for the tail plumes I'm thinking of them as thin flat ribbons swept along a path, tapering like trails of fire, with a narrow cross-section defined by small x/y radii.

I'm planning five tail plumes radiating from the hips, each a catmull-rom path curving down and outward with slightly different horizontal offsets to fan them out, colored with a gradient from crimson at the base to gold at the tip.

Now I'm sketching the body skeleton: a hips joint as the root, with a spine chain running up through a couple of midpoints to the shoulders, and a neck chain branching off the top of the spine.

The head joint hangs off the end of the neck, aimed forward and slightly upward, and I'm positioning a small sphere there to form the actual head shape with a bit of flattening on one axis.

Now I'm setting up the beak: a jaw joint anchored near the head's front-underside, and I'm sketching bezier curves for both the upper and lower beak halves using local offsets from the head and jaw joints so the sweep tapers from a wider base to a narrow tip.

For the eyes, I'll use amber glowing spheres with small dark pupils offset slightly forward, keeping things simple rather than using decals. For embers and sparks, I'm considering using textured cards with a glow sprite scattered deterministically around the wingtips, built from frames positioned so they face the camera.

Writing SVG spark texture...

For positioning sparks, I'm using a seeded random generator to scatter around 60 points with upward drift, spreading them in x, y, and z ranges to simulate rising embers above the wings.

I'm now setting up card sizing for sparks with slight size variation, and considering adding wing membranes connecting the shoulder chain to the wingtip path, making sure the edges run consistently root-to-tip.

For the membrane color, I'm sketching a gradient running crimson near the body to gold or orange at the tip, anchored at approximate body and tip coordinates. I'm defining the wing chain itself with named joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip) parented to the spine's mid-joint, then placing primary feathers along sampled points on the trailing-edge path to give the wing some visual depth.

Adding gradient from crimson to gold along each feather's length, plus a secondary row of smaller covert feathers near the elbow to bring the count to about six per wing. Now I'm defining the outline function that generates the flame-shaped point array for each feather.

Finishing the outline points, verifying it forms a valid non-intersecting polygon with a sharp tip, then moving on to extrude settings for thickness and bevel, crest flames using smaller versions of the same shape, and tail ribbons with a tapering box-section sweep.

For colors, I'm applying gradient paints across the body and tail that transition from crimson to orange or gold, giving a fire-like effect from tail to neck to head. I'm also checking the wing proportions and rescaling the shoulder-elbow-wrist-tip joint positions so the overall wingspan feels proportionate rather than oversized.

Now I'm defining the trailing edge points of the wing membrane and matching feather positions along the trail using interpolation, pulling feathers slightly above the membrane surface and attaching them to the nearest wing joint via a nearestJoint helper. For the mirrored wing, I'm flipping the x-coordinates of all these positions to generate the opposite side.

For the sparks, I'm thinking through how the frame function orients each spark card — using an upward facing axis with default flow so the sprite stands correctly — and planning to add a density of around 40 sparks plus surrounding embers.

Now I'm scattering the sparks around the wing area with randomized positions and sizing, using an rng helper to vary each one's size and spin. Then I move on to the amber glowing eyes, adding a small sphere element for each.

Next I'm placing dark pupils offset slightly forward from the eyes, then shaping the head as a sphere positioned near the top of the neck, deciding on an orange/gold color scheme rather than a full gradient. I settle on a flat color palette (crimson, red, orange, gold, amber, beak, dark tones) and start setting up the module's imports and exports for the builder function.

Writing joint and chain code...

Still building the head geometry and features...

Placing the crest flames along the top-back of the head, tilting them backward with a tilted plane direction, and setting thickness and width so they extrude as flame-like shapes rising from the skull.

Actually simpler: five flames arranged in a row with lateral offsets, center one longest and tallest, tapering outward, all extruded in the same tilted plane with a red-to-gold gradient coloring from base to tip.

Now I'm setting up the wings as catmull-rom chains on each side using a mirrored helper, defining shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip joints parented to the spine, then moving on to building the trail points.

I'm adding the membrane connecting the wing and trail with a gold-to-red gradient, and generating a row of flame-shaped primary feathers along the trail that shrink closer to the body and attach to the nearest wing joint.

For additional detail, I'm considering small covert feathers near the wing's leading edge, then moving on to building the tail plumes as five swept curved paths fanning outward from center.

Still placing ember cards...

Checking part counts stay reasonable—feathers, crest, and merged card parts all fine. Writing the flame outline function and setting up the head part with its orange color, bone attachment, and scale.

Defining flame outline points...

Verifying the crest tip offset calculation and confirming all the needed imports (frame, rng, THREE) are actually used.
